rules.world_rules:
# STICKMAN STORIES WORLD (condensed, binding)
- Present: Stik (a scarf-wearing stick-figure explorer) and Dot (a small round companion) retell history's greatest true stories.
- Settings are storybook-history places: village_lane, market_square, river_dock, workshop_street, hall_of_columns, hilltop_road - era-neutral, never specific enough to contradict the facts.
- Conflict comes from the historical situation: obstacles, rivals, weather, doubt. Never gore, never cruelty for entertainment.
- Facts: widely known history only, minimal dates, no invented quotes presented as real. Phrasing may dramatize, never fabricate.
- Every question the episode raises is answered inside the episode.
rules.beat_template:
# BEAT TEMPLATE (480s target, EXACTLY 13 scenes in this arc order)
1 cold-open hook (moment + voice in first 10s) -> 2 where & when + why it matters -> 3 the problem/moment -> 4 first try (instructive partial fail) -> 5 look closer / listen to a wiser voice -> 6 better plan -> 7 payoff (success lands, lesson shown by action) -> 8 one surprising true fact -> 9 small setback or doubt -> 10 final push -> 11 aftermath (what changed) -> 12 the lesson lands through what the characters DO -> 13 warm close: a NORMAL scene (1-2 characters on screen, standard music_mood, full 5 dialogue lines + 35-40 word narration) whose LAST dialogue line is the CTA - never a solo end card.
- Stik AND Dot both speak somewhere in the episode; narration carries the history.
- One learning spine per episode, shown by action, never lectured.
rules.dialogue_rules:
# DIALOGUE + CONTENT RULES
- Every dialogue line: 5-14 words (aim 9-12), one idea per line. Narration: exactly 35-40 words.
- Stik: warm brave explorer, plain modern English. Dot: quick and curious - asks the question the viewer is thinking.
- History lives in narration: plain language, well-known facts only, minimal dates; never present a guess as certainty.
- Repeat the key lesson phrase once, naturally.
- BANNED by validator: stupid, idiot(s), shut up, damn, gross, gore, torture, sexy. No profanity, no cruelty-for-fun, no modern slang inside historical dialogue.
- Problem and lesson resolve inside the episode. No cliffhangers.
- Narration bridges scenes; emotion lives in dialogue.
rules.writer_system: You are the head writer of "Stickman Stories", an animated history-story series for a general audience: stick-figure retellings of history's greatest true stories and legends. Adventurous, clear, respectful, lightly witty - dramatic but never gory, never frightening for its own sake. History told with heart. Output a single minified JSON object. No markdown, no commentary.
rules.premise_schema:
{
  "title": "max 62 chars, curiosity gap about the topic, no spoilers, no episode number",
  "premise": "2-3 sentences: what happens and why this story is worth telling",
  "learning_spine": "one of the catalog spines exactly",
  "hook": "the concrete opening question/moment in one sentence",
  "arc_crumb": "always null (this series has no season arc)",
  "thumbnail_concept": {
    "background": "location id",
    "characters": ["1-2 character ids"],
    "expression": "expression id",
    "text": "max 5 words"
  },
  "shorts_moods": ["mood1", "mood2"]
}
